significance.justification: Verified true, the conclusion would be that scores on “external-modality predictivity, cross-dataset stability, and causal ablation specificity” jointly predict whether an orphan SAE feature will independently confirm as scientific signal rather than artifact; this is a form-(iii) predictive coupling between measurable criteria and later confirmation. It would fix expectations for unseen orphan features and decisions about follow-up, addressing the validation gap exposed by annotation-enrichment and auto-description workflows such as InterPLM, while establishing a phenomenon and reusable discriminator rather than showing that the features themselves instantiate established scientific mechanisms. Verified false would determinately rule out this proposed three-criterion coupling as a general triage basis, although it would not rule out other discriminators or the existence of genuine orphan signals. In the topic-substitution check, the generic topic alone would not warrant this score: the prospective signal-versus-artifact law is materially more constraining than the median hypothesis that model features align with known scientific concepts.

reach.justification: The named handle is the “logistic-regression triage classifier” built from the three criterion scores, presented as a “ranked prioritizer” or hard filter for orphan features. It is explicitly ex ante: a practitioner uses it “before committing wet-lab or downstream-enrichment follow-up,” leaving an action window in which expensive validation can be prioritized or avoided. The hypothesis asserts applicability to “any scientific FM,” and after per-model feature extraction the claimed relation predicts which high-scoring orphans should externally confirm, so more than a model-specific direction survives recalibration; downstream users include scientific-model auditors and researchers allocating experimental follow-up. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score, because the broad topic supplies neither this prospective handle nor its cross-modal predictive relation.
